links.note: In 1415 the Council of Constance named a vicar general over the Observant friars of France, Burgundy and Touraine. In 1443 Pope Eugenius IV confirmed two vicars general for the Observants, one for each side of the Alps. The head of the Franciscans had named them at the pope's wish. In 1446 the pope ruled that the Observants would elect their own vicars general every three years. He said he was following rules of the Council of Constance and of Pope Martin V.
links.outcome: In 1446 Pope Eugenius IV ruled that the Observants would choose their own leaders, and the head of the order had to confirm them.

prose_changes.old: The Rule became the standard for monks in the West. Carolingian reformers made it the norm across the Frankish empire. It stands behind the Cluniacs, the Cistercians and the Benedictine congregations that keep it today. Its language of stability, obedience and moderation reached far beyond the cloister. So did the way it built the day around fixed hours of prayer, and both passed into the West's habits of work and time. Monte Cassino itself was destroyed again and again, and rebuilt every time. Paul the Deacon tells how the Lombards sacked it. The abbey's own medieval chronicle tells of a Saracen attack. An earthquake later brought it down, and in 1944 Allied bombing destroyed it. Monks live there now.
prose_changes.new: The Rule became the standard for monks in the West. Carolingian reformers made it the norm across the Frankish empire. It stands behind the Cluniacs, the Cistercians and the Benedictine congregations that keep it today. Its language of stability, obedience and moderation reached far beyond the cloister. So did the way it built the day around fixed hours of prayer, and both passed into the West's habits of work and time. Monte Cassino itself was destroyed again and again, and rebuilt every time. Paul the Deacon tells how the Lombards sacked it. The abbey's own medieval chronicle tells of a Saracen attack. An earthquake later brought it down, and Allied bombing in 1944 is reported to have destroyed it. Monks live there now.
